ca_happy_boulder.blurb: Happy Boulder is the centrepiece of the central canyon in the Happy Boulders, a wash cut into the volcanic tablelands north of Bishop in the Eastern Sierra. The 14 problems cover a wide range, from the easiest grades up to a pair of V9s, with the harder lines concentrated on the south face and a few gentle problems on the north side that suit a warm-up. Holds are generally positive, and the sheltered wash feels warmer than the open Buttermilks on a cold, windy day. It is a short stroll past the neighbouring Solarium Boulder, and the mixed grade spread makes it a good stop for groups with varied abilities.

ca_kimball_canyon_crag.blurb: This crag is a high rhyolite plug with steep flanks, in Robert Louis Stevenson State Park on Mt. St. Helena, in the Napa wine country. Nearly all of the 14 routes are bolted sport lines, ranging from 5.10 to the low 5.12s, with most clustering in the 5.11 range; there is nothing easy here. Expect steep, well-protected climbing on jugs, crimps, edges and pockets. The north-facing lines stay shaded most of the day, which is welcome in summer heat, while the canyon can turn cold and windy in winter. The hike in is long and uphill, so this is a committed outing rather than a quick lap session.

ca_main_wall_14.blurb: Main Wall is a short bouldering face just south of the Cliff House on San Francisco's Ocean Beach, reached by walking along the sand to the area below the totem pole. It holds 14 problems, most of them in the easy to moderate range from V0 into the V3 and V5 territory, with a handful of much harder lines topping out at the high end of the scale. A few lines have anchors for anyone who would rather not climb a tall highball without a rope. This is an urban, beachside spot where the tide and sand level decide how comfortable the landings are, so check conditions and bring a pad.

ca_perpetual_motion_wall.blurb: This lengthy wall faces southeast and sits in the Virgin Islands area off Geology Tour Road in Joshua Tree National Park, a quieter corner of the park with lighter crowds. Nearly all of its 14 routes are trad crack climbs, running from easy fifth class up through the 5.10s and into 5.11, with the namesake overhanging hand crack as the standout. Expect a rugged, scenic setting above a valley ringed by big boulders. The walk in is rough and takes roughly 20 to 30 minutes depending on which route you want, and the face is not visible until you are nearly there.

ca_murphy_creek.blurb: Murphy Creek is a small granite crag near Tenaya Lake in the Tuolumne Meadows part of Yosemite National Park, at roughly 8,300 feet. The 14 routes are mostly trad cracks, from an easy double crack in the 5.7 range up through the 5.10s and 5.11s to one 5.12, plus a top-rope option. Gear can feel sparse on some of the easier lines, so bring a generous rack. The hike is easy, crossing open granite slabs before a cross-country finish to the only sheer cliff in sight. It makes a handy escape from the crowds and the heat of the valley floor in summer.

ca_fictitioua_tree_rock.blurb: Fictitioua Tree Rock is a small crag off the Angeles Crest Highway in the Angeles National Forest above Los Angeles, often called a mini Joshua Tree. Most of its 14 routes are mellow trad lines on gritty rock with flaring hand and finger cracks, flakes, knobs, a chimney and some slab, with a pair of aid lines as well. Grades run from easy scrambles through the 5.7 to 5.9 range up to a few 5.11s. Anchors on top allow top-roping, and an easy walk-up on one side reaches the summit. It is a quiet spot for quick laps, far from the crowds and heat of the desert.
ca_fictitioua_tree_rock.parking_note: Drive up the Angeles Crest Highway and turn left onto Sulphur Springs Road about a mile beyond Newcomb's Ranch. The Three Points trailhead lot is right after the turn.

ca_rock_hudson.blurb: Rock Hudson is a large formation in the Outback section of Joshua Tree National Park, a short walk northeast of Hidden Valley Campground. Its 14 routes are almost all trad cracks and face climbs, from beginner-friendly lines through a cluster of 5.10s to a few 5.11s and one low-5.12 edge route, with a single aid route and a top-rope problem mixed in. Most climbs sit on the sunny southwest side, so expect plenty of sun, though a few lines face north or east. The west face holds a classic widening crack that finishes in a chimney.

ca_tahquitz_ice_surrounding_flows.blurb: These are the winter water-ice and mixed flows on and around Tahquitz Rock and Suicide Rock above Idyllwild in Southern California. Most of the 14 listed routes are around WI3, with a few easier lines, and one much harder flow up near the top of the scale. Some run to several hundred feet or more, and unless the ice is very fat, many climb as mixed routes. The ice is unreliable: it takes heavy snowfall followed by cold nights and freeze-thaw cycles, and it does not form every winter. Parties start very early, since daytime warmth thaws the flows. The Trough is the most consistent of them, at about 500 feet.
